thesis: The higher-frequency trend-dip entry can retain its positive base expectancy under stressed costs when paired with the wider 100-basis-point stop and 200-basis-point target observed in the cost-resilient sparse variant.
rationale: The first formal trend-dip experiment separated two useful observations: a 103-trade rule with positive base returns but excessive tight-stop costs, and a 36-trade rule with positive 1.5x-cost returns at a 100/200 risk envelope. This immutable anchor combines only those previously observed design choices before any new final-test read.
